content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of the RENEWAL review for Clear Capital (counterparty RadialSpark, LLC):**

**Renewal mechanics — no issue.** This is an evergreen MSA, not a term-and-renewal deal:
- § 2 (p0011): term runs from signing "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6."
- § 6(a) (p0032): either party may exit for any or no reason on 15 days' notice.
- A document-wide search for "renew" returns zero hits — no automatic renewal, no successive/multi-year renewal term, no non-renewal notice window. Nothing near the walk-away triggers (>90-day window or auto multi-year renewal), and the 15-day exit is actually easier than our preferred 30-day opt-out.

**Pricing predictability — deviation flagged.** § 3(b) (p0014) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped right to change rates on 30 days' notice. In an evergreen deal this is the functional equivalent of renewal uplift, and it bites harder than usual here because:
- the § 6(a) convenience exit exists only when "there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," so Clear Capital cannot walk away from a mid-SOW increase; and
- compensation is time-and-materials at SOW rates (p0013), so an increase flows straight through with no cap on size or frequency.

**Redline (validated `ok:true`).** Smallest possible edit — the 30-day notice bargain is left untouched, and I only appended the playbook cap: increases no more than once per 12 months, limited to the lesser of CPI and 3%, with rates in an already-executed SOW fixed for that SOW's duration. The comment offers the 5% fallback if RadialSpark pushes back.

One judgment call worth surfacing: the rule's title centers on auto-renewal and notice windows, and neither exists here, so a narrower reading would have closed this as compliant. I flagged it because the rule's stated purpose ("priced predictably"), its detection guidance ("price uplift language") and its redline guidance ("cap uplift") all reach the uplift lever, and passing an uncapped unilateral increase that we cannot exit mid-SOW would leave real customer exposure unaddressed. Confidence is 0.68 to reflect that scoping question — if your playbook has a separate standalone pricing/rate-increase rule, this item likely belongs there instead and should be de-duplicated.
